rubric.why: Shows that an enzyme lowers the activation energy by forming an enzyme-substrate complex or providing a lower-energy pathway.
rubric.description: Explains how an enzyme lowers activation energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the enzyme-substrate complex or for an alternative pathway that requires lower activation energy.

rubric.why: The question asks for two factors affecting enzyme activity.
rubric.description: Names any two valid factors affecting enzyme activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two different valid factors.

modelAnswer: An enzyme binds with its substrate to form an enzyme substrate complex, providing an alternative pathway that requires lower activation energy.
Two factors affecting enzyme activity are temperature and pH.

items.followUp: Describe how an enzyme-substrate complex forms and name two factors that affect enzyme activity.

rubric.why: The induced-fit model describes a substrate binding to an enzyme's flexible active site.
rubric.description: States that the substrate binds to a flexible active site.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing substrate binding to the enzyme's flexible active site.

rubric.why: Substrate binding induces a change in the enzyme's shape, improving the fit.
rubric.description: Explains that binding changes the enzyme's shape so the active site fits the substrate closely.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the induced shape change and improved fit.

modelAnswer: In the induced-fit model, the enzyme's active site is flexible and is not a perfect fit for the substrate before binding.
When the substrate binds, it induces a shape change in the enzyme, so the active site fits the substrate closely.
